Compile a spec into the reference frame npmatch matches against

Source: R/md-compile.R
md_compile.Rd

Turns an md_spec() into the wide np_reference frame: one row per EIN x selected name x paired address, with npmatch's derived columns, .ein, .id and active (PLAN.md section 6). It also returns the corpus statistics for exactly that selection, and a report of what the selection emits and what it leaves out.

Usage

md_compile(
  spec,
  con = NULL,
  derive = c("stored", "normalize", "none"),
  max_rows = 2e+07,
  check_rows = 2000L
)

Arguments

spec

An md_spec().

con

A connection from md_db().

derive

"stored" (the npmatch frame from stored columns), "normalize" (the same frame, by running np_normalize()) or "none" (raw fields only).

max_rows

Row budget. Emission is counted before anything is materialised, and a spec over budget is an error naming the classes responsible, rather than a reference that costs far more than planned.

check_rows

For derive = "stored", how many rows to re-normalize and compare. 0 skips the check.

Value

An object of class md_reference: reference (the frame), name_freq, token_idf, name_eins, token_df, n_name_rows, report, spec and stamp.

Where the rows come from

Names come from name_compact: one row per (ein, name_key), collapsed across sources, without in-care-of names or guarded observed rows. Addresses come from address and address_derived, collapsed here over the selected classes to one row per place - address_compact has no variant class to select on.

The pairing rule

Section 8: a third party wrote an observed name together with an address, so an observed name pairs with the observed addresses written beside it (address.name_id), and only first-party names cross with first-party addresses. Emission is then roughly names + addresses per EIN, not their product. An observed name with no address of its own pairs with the EIN's first-party addresses; an EIN with no selected address still gets one row per name, with the address fields empty.

Derived columns

Every column npmatch::np_normalize() adds is a function of one input field, and md_build_derived() stores all of them. derive = "stored" (the default) gives each row the stored columns of a row holding exactly its strings - the name row with its spelling, the address row with its street, zip and state, the DBA row with its DBA - so the frame is what np_normalize() would build, without running it. A sample of check_rows rows is then re-normalized and compared, and any difference is an error. derive = "normalize" runs np_normalize() on the whole frame instead.

Either way the installed normalizer must be the one that built name_derived, because name_compact's keys came from it.

Statistics

Two kinds, both returned:

name_freq, token_idf

npmatch's own, over the emitted frame - what npmatch::np_cascade() uses today. A name repeated once per paired address counts once per row.

name_eins, token_df, n_name_rows

over names, one per (ein, name_key). For a spec without a cross-cutting filter these are summed from md_build_stats()'s cells; otherwise computed directly from the selected names. report$stats_method says which.

The report

Shape: rows by name and address class, rows per EIN, EINs with no address. Absence (section 8a): for each cluster type, how many selected EINs have a family member the selection leaves out. A thin reference cannot see the sibling it is missing, and auto-accepts against whichever member it holds; this is the count that says how often that can happen.
